builder_plan.scenario: Your workload might fit a smaller or differently structured model.
builder_plan.change: Check for available weights and a compatible runtime before planning a product trial.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Does Scaling Toward AGI Depend on What System-1 Lets System-2 Execute?
summary: The paper proposes replacing unconditional execution of all candidate interactions (reasoning steps, tool calls, agent actions) by a large expensive model with a predict-gate-execute-update loop in which a lightweight learned predictor estimates candidate utility and an adaptive threshold admits only high-value candidates for costly execution. The cost is training and maintaining the System-1 predictor, managing threshold calibration and online updates, plus added pipeline complexity, with possible quality loss on gated-out candidates bounded by predictor error and the utility margin. It can fail when predictor errors are large, utility margins are small, exploration is underfunded, or distribution shift degrades the screener, eroding the theoretical savings; the paper is a conceptual framework with bounds rather than a validated implementation.
rationale: This is a theoretical framework with no released system or measured gains, so a constrained-infrastructure team should monitor the idea of utility gating rather than adopt it now.
technique: Predict-gate-execute loop with lightweight utility screener

claims.statement: The paper proposes replacing unconditional execution of all candidate interactions (reasoning steps, tool calls, agent actions) by a large expensive model with a predict-gate-execute-update loop in which a lightweight learned predictor estimates candidate utility and an adaptive threshold admits only high-value candidates for costly execution. The cost is training and maintaining the System-1 predictor, managing threshold calibration and online updates, plus added pipeline complexity, with possible quality loss on gated-out candidates bounded by predictor error and the utility margin. It can fail when predictor errors are large, utility margins are small, exploration is underfunded, or distribution shift degrades the screener, eroding the theoretical savings; the paper is a conceptual framework with bounds rather than a validated implementation.

Under ideal screening and equal execution costs, execution compute falls by a factor approaching 1/rho_u, where rho_u is the density of utility-relevant interactions; no empirical factor is reported because rho_u is workload-dependent and unmeasured.
